with_overlay_glaucoma.prompt:
You are a senior ophthalmologist. You are analyzing a fundus photograph from a patient with glaucoma. In this image, the optic disc have been pre-segmented.
        Provide a thorough clinical description of the image, using the terminology and style of a glaucoma specialist. Your description should mention relevant findings if any exists.
        After your description, provide a structured classification using exactly these fields and options:
        Cup-to-Disc Ratio (CDR): 0 – ≤0.3 (normal); 1 – 0.4–0.5 (borderline); 2 – 0.6–0.7 (suspicious); 3 – 0.8–0.9 (advanced cupping); 4 – 1.0 (total cupping)
        Neuroretinal Rim: 0 – Normal (ISNT rule preserved: Inferior ≥ Superior ≥ Nasal ≥ Temporal); 1 – ISNT rule violation; 2 – Focal notching; 3 – Diffuse thinning; 4 – Near-total or total rim loss
        Disc Hemorrhage (Drance Hemorrhage): 0 – None; 1 – Present (splinter hemorrhage at or near disc margin)
        Peripapillary Atrophy (PPA): 0 – None; 1 – Beta-zone PPA only; 2 – Large or progressive beta-zone PPA
        Retinal Nerve Fiber Layer (RNFL) Defect: 0 – No visible defect; 1 – Wedge-shaped defect; 2 – Diffuse thinning; 3 – Both wedge defect and diffuse thinning
        Optic Disc Pallor: 0 – Normal color; 1 – Mild pallor; 2 – Significant pallor (consider other optic neuropathies)
        Vessel Changes: 0 – Normal vessel pattern; 1 – Bayoneting (vessels deflect at rim edge); 2 – Nasalization of vessels; 3 – Both bayoneting and nasalization   
        Format your response in two parts: (1) the free-text clinical description, and (2) the structured classification with the selected option for each field.
